blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — An analysis by the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME) found that bacterial infections involving antimicrobial resistance (AMR) were associated with an estimated 51,800 deaths in the Philippines in 2021, including 13,000 deaths directly attributable to drug resistance. The figures illustrate the growing difficulty of treating infections when medicines intended to kill disease-causing germs or stop them from multiplying no longer work as expected. AMR occurs when bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites develop the ability to survive medicines designed to kill them or stop them from multiplying.
